lens: The referee who wants to reject. No stake in the work and a low opinion of in-silico oncology: reading for the sentence that lets me say 'this does not show what it claims to show' — a conclusion one notch stronger than the method licenses, a missing control, an unexamined confound, an alternative explanation the paper never names, a forbidden implication of efficacy/safety/window/selectivity/readiness, and a limitation phrased so a reader skims past it.
what_i_read: research/modalities/emc_atr_vulnerability.py (at the pin: derive_part_b, the _contrast/_adj_contrast Welch calls, _platform_readable, _rank_key, the _pool threshold block, derive_part_c, collect_part_d/derive_part_d, grade)

research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json (at the pin: part_a_hemcss_identity in full; part_d_drug_response_correlation.gdsc_meta, ._fet_signature_design, .fet_signature, .correlations per drug per predictor)
central_claim: The published FET-fusion -> suppressed-ATM -> compensatory-ATR-dependency hypothesis is not supported by any computable evidence that it transfers to EMC: EMC tumour transcriptomes carry no DDR signal that survives adjustment for generic proliferation (two series), the CRISPR dependency readout is saturated and cannot discriminate, and ATR-inhibitor sensitivity fails three of four pre-registered mechanism tests including the mechanism's own load-bearing variable — so the hypothesis is bounded on three sides and is neither supported nor refuted, while the wet-lab ask, which rests on sequence arguments rather than on these correlations, is unchanged.

blockers.summary: The paper's ONLY positive result is claimed to demonstrate target specificity, and the number that contradicts that reading sits unreported in the same artifact. §5 says of the passing test: 'two independent instruments — a genetic knockout and a chemical inhibitor, ON THE SAME TARGET, in the same lines — agree about which lines care. It says the drug acts on the target it is named for.' The same predictor (mean ATR+ATRIP+CHEK1 CRISPR gene effect) correlates with MK-1775 / adavosertib — a WEE1 inhibitor, not an ATR inhibitor — at rho = +0.157 (n 601), which sits INSIDE the range of the two ATR inhibitors it is claimed to be specific to (azd6738 +0.252 n 597; ve-822 +0.173 n 565). MK-1775 is in the committed artifact's `drugs_with_data`, is flagged `is_atr_inhibitor: false`, is not one of the paper's non-DDR controls, and is named nowhere in the manuscript. The data therefore supports the weaker claim — lines dependent on the ATR-CHK1-WEE1 replication-checkpoint module are more sensitive to drugs targeting that module — and not the claim printed, which is about the named target of one drug class. This is the exact 'one notch stronger than the method licenses' failure, in the single result the paper offers as passing.
blockers.evidence: research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json#part_d_drug_response_correlation.correlations['mk-1775'].by_predictor['dependency::ATR_ATRIP_CHEK1_mean_gene_effect'] = {rho: 0.1571, n: 601}, against ['azd6738'] rho 0.2520 n 597 and ['ve-822'] rho 0.1726 n 565; .gdsc_meta.drugs_with_data lists mk-1775; research/modalities/emc_atr_vulnerability.py line 2839 `non_ddr_controls = ("paclitaxel", "bortezomib", "doxorubicin")` — mk-1775 is neither an ATRi nor a control and is collected but never used; grep of the manuscript at the pin for 'mk-1775|adavosertib' returns 0 hits.
blockers.fix: Print the MK-1775 row in §5's table beside the two ATR inhibitors, and replace 'on the same target … It says the drug acts on the target it is named for' with what the three numbers support: 'a genetic knockout of the ATR-CHK1 module and chemical inhibitors of that module agree about which lines care — including a WEE1 inhibitor at rho +0.157, so this is module-level consistency, not evidence of ATR-specific engagement.' The pre-registered PASS itself survives that rewrite; only the interpretive sentence changes.

p1s.summary: The drug-specificity bar — one of four pre-registered bars — is computed as a MEAN over two control drugs whose correlations have opposite signs and similar magnitude, so a control value near zero is produced by cancellation rather than by absence of association. Replication-stress expression is printed 'vs non-DDR drugs +0.037 ✅': the two controls are bortezomib +0.2196 and paclitaxel −0.1462. The held-out FET signature is printed '+0.062 ✅': bortezomib +0.2645 and paclitaxel −0.1413. In the FET row the LARGEST drug association anywhere in the panel is bortezomib at +0.265 — bigger than the ATR-inhibitor association (−0.138) it is being tested against — and the ✅ says the opposite. ⭑ FAIR NOTE, and it matters: for the one row where specificity is load-bearing (the passing CRISPR predictor) both controls are individually near zero (bortezomib +0.0213, paclitaxel +0.0070), so no verdict in the paper changes. The two ✅ marks are unearned, not the conclusions built on them.
p1s.fix: Print the per-control-drug rho, not the mean, and change the specificity rule to require EVERY control drug to be below the bar. Where a control exceeds the ATRi association in magnitude — bortezomib for the FET signature — say so in the sentence rather than in an averaged column.

p1s.summary: Per-drug detail is given for the test that passes and withheld for the three that fail, and the paper's single most-repeated negative is a mean of two values that differ sevenfold. 'rho = −0.090, the wrong sign' (headline, §5 twice, §6.3) is the mean of azd6738 −0.0224 (n 704, t −0.595, i.e. an unambiguous null) and ve-822 −0.1583 (n 656, t −4.10). For AZD6738 the ATM predictor has no sign to be wrong about. The same averaging hides that replication-stress expression is −0.088 for one ATR inhibitor and −0.239 for the other — a difference larger than the gap the paper adjudicates between predictors. The asymmetry (per-drug rho printed only for the PASS: 'rho +0.252 … and +0.173') is the shape a referee reads as reporting the detail that flatters and the average that does not.
p1s.evidence: research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json#part_d_drug_response_correlation.correlations['azd6738'|'ve-822'].by_predictor['expr::ATM_signalling_DSB_repair'] = −0.0224 (n 704) / −0.1583 (n 656), mean −0.0904; ['expr::replication_stress'] = −0.0879 / −0.2394, mean −0.164; manuscript §5 prints per-drug values only in the ✅ paragraph.
p1s.fix: Give §5's table a per-drug rho column for all four predictors. Then rewrite 'the wrong sign' — with one drug at −0.02 and one at −0.16, the honest sentence is 'the mechanism's load-bearing predictor reaches the pre-registered magnitude bar on neither ATR inhibitor, and on neither does it move in the predicted direction.'

p1s.summary: The quantitative decision rule that produces the paper's headline tier is never printed. §3.4 says 'Three DDR concepts clear the raw threshold' and §6.1's predicate table repeats it; the threshold's VALUE appears nowhere in the document. It is Δ > 0.2 in within-sample SD units, applied to a mean of deltas across the readable platforms of the chosen series, with a companion rule that no more than one unrelated control set may also clear it. §1 asserts 'the grading, fixed before the numbers and reported verbatim … so that neither can be softened after the fact' — but the verbatim text reproduced is qualitative ('EMC tumours show the … signature'), and every operative constant (0.2; the ≤1 control rule; ≥8 genes per concept; ≥3 EMC and ≥3 comparators per platform) lives only in code. A reader given adjusted values of +0.128, +0.074 and +0.062 has no rule with which to check that they fail.
p1s.evidence: research/modalities/emc_atr_vulnerability.py lines 2309-2322: `ddr_up_raw = [c for c in tested if raw.get(c, {}).get('mean_delta_across_readable_platforms', 0) > 0.2]`, `d['signature_specific_to_DDR'] = bool(ddr_up_adj) and len(ctrl_up) <= 1`; line 2005 `if len(genes) < 8: continue`; lines 2108-2114 `_platform_readable`. Manuscript grep for '0.2 ' as a threshold: absent.
p1s.fix: Add one sentence to §1 or §3.4 stating the numbers: 'a concept counts as elevated at Δ > 0.2 within-sample SD units, and the signature counts as DDR-specific only if at least one DDR concept clears 0.2 after proliferation adjustment while at most one unrelated control set clears it raw.' No result changes; the rule becomes checkable.

p1s.summary: Tumour purity and cellularity — the first thing a sarcoma pathologist would raise about this comparison — is not mentioned anywhere in the document. EMC is a hypocellular myxoid tumour with abundant extracellular matrix; the GSE4303 comparators are GIST and DFSP and the GSE24369 comparators are LGFMS, desmoid and fibrosarcoma. Bulk transcriptomes of EMC are systematically more diluted by non-tumour material, which attenuates every cell-intrinsic, cycle-linked signal — including the DDR and proliferation scores whose RATIO carries the whole verdict. The confound points in the direction of the paper's own null, so it is an alternative explanation for the central Part B result and the paper never names it. There is no purity estimate, no cellularity covariate and no stroma control set.
p1s.evidence: manuscript §3.4 (comparator composition and the raw/adjusted table) and §3.2 (gene sets: no stromal, ECM or immune set among the four 'unrelated controls' — Myogenesis, Adipogenesis, OxPhos, DNA Repair); no occurrence of 'purity', 'cellularity', 'stroma' or 'myxoid matrix' anywhere in the document at the pin.
p1s.fix: Add a named limitation in §3.4 and carry it into §6.1: 'these are bulk tumour transcriptomes with no purity estimate; EMC's myxoid, hypocellular architecture is expected to dilute cell-intrinsic signals relative to the comparators, and this analysis cannot separate that dilution from a genuinely absent DDR signature.' Cheaply strengthened by scoring a stromal/ECM set alongside the existing controls.

p1s.summary: The interpretation of the control gene sets does not match what the control gene sets are. §3.4 concludes: 'the two UNRELATED control sets (oxphos, adipogenesis) move as much as or more than any DDR set. That is the signature of a growth-rate difference, not of a DDR mechanism.' Oxidative phosphorylation and adipogenesis are metabolic and lineage programmes, not proliferation programmes. Their movement (oxphos +0.384, t 3.95; adipogenesis +0.218, t 5.08 — both larger than any DDR term) is evidence of a broad, non-specific transcriptional offset between EMC and GIST/DFSP, most plausibly cell of origin and tissue composition. That reading undermines the RAW Δ values wholesale rather than attributing them to growth rate, and it is the same confound as the purity item above.
p1s.evidence: manuscript §3.4 GSE4303 table (oxphos +0.384/3.95, adipogenesis +0.218/5.08 vs the largest DDR term S-phase +0.311/4.46) and the sentence following it; §3.2 gene-set table assigns MYC targets and Mitotic Spindle as the proliferation controls and OxPhos/Adipogenesis/Myogenesis/DNA Repair as 'unrelated controls'.
p1s.fix: Replace 'That is the signature of a growth-rate difference' with 'unrelated metabolic and lineage sets move as much as the DDR sets, so the raw contrast is dominated by a non-specific difference between EMC and its comparators; only the proliferation-adjusted column is interpretable, and in it no DDR concept clears the threshold.' Stronger, and it is what the numbers say.

p1s.summary: Two nulls at n = 10 and n = 6 EMC tumours are reported without any statement of what effect they could have detected. §3.4 elevates their agreement to a result — 'That concordance is what makes this a result rather than a single series' quirk' — and §6.1 reports the WEAK tier 'as reached rather than as narrowly missed'. No minimum detectable effect, no power calculation, no confidence interval on any Δ appears in Part B. Two underpowered nulls agreeing is weak evidence of concordance and no evidence of adequacy, and 'absence of evidence' is exactly the objection this design invites.
p1s.evidence: manuscript §3.4 (GSE4303: 10 EMC vs 6 comparators; GSE24369: 6 EMC vs 29) and §6.1 ('part B is 16 EMC tumours on two microarrays'); research/modalities/emc_atr_vulnerability.py `_contrast` returns a bare Welch dict (delta, t) with no interval, and `_pool` averages deltas with no uncertainty.
p1s.fix: Report the minimum Δ detectable at 80% power on each series given the observed within-group SDs, in the same paragraph as the null. If the MDE is above the 0.2 threshold on GSE4303, that is the honest headline for that series and it should be stated.

p1s.summary: No correlation in Part D carries an interval, and one pass/fail turns on a difference of 0.007. §5 fails the replication-stress predictor because 'the plain proliferation control reaches −0.171, very slightly more' than its −0.164 — at n ≈ 700 the standard error on a single rho is ≈ 0.038, so the two are indistinguishable. The passing predictor is +0.212 against a bar of 0.15, and its weaker drug (ve-822, rho +0.173, n 565) has a Fisher-z 95% interval of roughly [+0.09, +0.25] — it straddles its own pre-registered bar. A referee will say the four-bar scheme is being applied as if the estimates were exact.
p1s.evidence: manuscript §5 table and the 'very slightly more' paragraph; research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json#part_d_drug_response_correlation.correlations['ve-822'].by_predictor['dependency::ATR_ATRIP_CHEK1_mean_gene_effect'] = {rho 0.1726, n 565} and ['azd6738'] = {rho 0.2520, n 597}; no interval field exists anywhere in the correlations block.
p1s.fix: Add a 95% Fisher-z interval to every rho in §5's table, and say in the text that a bar applied to point estimates cannot separate −0.164 from −0.171 — the argument that carries that row is the band argument the paper already makes (every expression predictor lands at −0.15 to −0.17), not the 0.007 gap.

p1s.summary: The document's most consequential single finding rests on a database annotation whose primary source was never opened. §2 turns on the Cellosaurus caution 'Does not harbor a gene fusion involving EWSR1 … (PubMed=34413129)', and the committed artifact records only the Cellosaurus record — there is no fetch of PMID 34413129 and no statement of what that paper measured, on how many lines, by what assay. §2 is the section that triggers corrections in six repository documents including an outward-facing one. Fetching a PubMed abstract is a $0 observation, which this repository's own evidence rules say must be taken rather than deferred.
p1s.evidence: research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json#part_a_hemcss_identity.cellosaurus.record.CC carries the caution string and nothing else; the artifact has no key naming 34413129 outside that string; manuscript §2.1 quotes the caution and never characterises the primary source.
p1s.fix: Fetch and cite PMID 34413129 — assay, cohort, and what it says about H-EMC-SS — in §2.1, and record it in the artifact. If the primary source turns out to be an incidental remark rather than a targeted test, §2's strength changes and the document should say so.

p1s.summary: The literature corroboration in §2.1 is confounded by gene aliasing and the paper does not say so. 'Of 21 Europe PMC records naming H-EMC-SS, exactly one mentions NR4A3' is offered as incidental corroboration. NR4A3 was named CHN, TEC, NOR-1, MINOR and CSMF through the period most H-EMC-SS literature was published, and the EWSR1 fusion was originally described as EWS-CHN/EWS-TEC. A search on the modern symbol over a corpus that is largely pre-2004 would return close to one hit whether or not the line carries the fusion, so the observation has almost no discriminating power as run.
p1s.evidence: manuscript §2.1 ⭑ paragraph ('Of 21 Europe PMC records naming H-EMC-SS, exactly one mentions NR4A3'); the artifact's part_a literature block records the query as run — the aliases are absent from it, while the same module's own DepMap fusion check does carry an alias-aware field (`calls_naming_any_NR4A3_alias`), so the asymmetry is internal.
p1s.fix: Re-run the Europe PMC query with CHN / TEC / NOR-1 / NOR1 / MINOR / CSMF added, or delete the sentence. If it is kept unre-run, state the alias limitation in the same sentence — a corroboration whose search cannot see the historical name of the gene is not corroboration.

p1s.summary: Two claims in §8 are stated more strongly than the evidence read supports. (a) §8.2 Q2: 'The first EMC sample ever to appear in an ATR-directed dataset' — an unqualified universal over all deposited data, from a bounded search of five archives. (b) §8.4: the USZ group 'framed selection on HRD, WITH THE EMC MODEL OUTSIDE THE BIOMARKER ANALYSIS' — a statement about the contents of a paper whose full text the document says twice it could not read ('not open access, so only the abstract was read'; §8.5.4 'its full text is paywalled'). What is actually known is that the EMC model is absent from the deposit's verbatim `overall_design`, which is a fact about GEO metadata, not about the paper's analysis.
p1s.evidence: manuscript §8.2 Q2 evidence cell; §8.4 point 3; §8.1 publication row ('not open access, so only the abstract was read') and §8.5 item 4 ('its full text is paywalled').
p1s.fix: (a) 'the first EMC sample we can find in any ATR-directed deposit — across the five archives searched in §3.0a'. (b) 'the deposit's own stated design accounts for the 62 tumours and does not include the EMC model; whether the paper's biomarker analysis includes it cannot be determined from the abstract.'

p1s.summary: A clinical-actionability word appears in the document's own voice. §8.2: 'Both programmes arrive at ATR as THE ACTIONABLE NODE in sarcoma; they nominate incompatible upstream lesions…'. This is not inside a quotation and not attributed — it asserts that ATR is actionable in sarcoma, which is a clinical-readiness claim of exactly the kind the banner at line 30 and §6.2 forbid. The surrounding text is careful; this clause is not.
p1s.evidence: manuscript §8.2, the sentence beginning '⛔ So this is a COMPETING BIOMARKER HYPOTHESIS'; contrast with the top banner ('No efficacy, potency, dose, safety, therapeutic-window or clinical-readiness claim is made or implied anywhere in this document') and §8's own producer block, which repeats it.
p1s.fix: 'Both programmes NOMINATE ATR as their target node in sarcoma; neither nomination is evaluated here.' One word plus a clause.

p1s.summary: Clinical and epidemiological numbers are printed without citations, in a document with seven citations total and no reference list. Uncited: '~5–11 % of EMC carries no identified FET partner' (§2.2); 'type 2 (EWSR1 exon 7::NR4A3 exon 2, SECOND-COMMONEST)' and 'type 1 … THE ACTUAL COMMONEST EMC fusion' (§0). Uncited instruments: DepMap 24Q4 and its CRISPR gene-effect scoring, GDSC2 8.5, Cellosaurus, Salmon (§8.1), Enrichr's underlying MSigDB/Reactome releases beyond the four method papers already given.
p1s.evidence: manuscript grep for 'PMID|et al|doi:' returns 7 lines total (Milacic, Ashburner, Liberzon, Kuleshov, Planas-Paz, Gracilla, and the superseded Menon row); §2.2's prevalence range and §0's fusion-frequency claims appear on lines carrying no citation; there is no References section.
p1s.fix: Cite the prevalence and fusion-frequency figures to a primary source or an authority, add primary citations for DepMap, GDSC2, Cellosaurus, Chronos and Salmon, and add a reference list. The repository's own rule is that everything clinical is cited and no identifier is written from recollection.

p1s.summary: The headline omits the document's own most consequential external finding, and it points the other way. 'THE HEADLINE — both halves' ends at '⭐ So: THE ASK SURVIVES; ITS COMPUTED SUPPORT IS WEAKER THAN FIRST REPRESENTED', with 'Half two: the ASK is unaffected … and this is not a consolation clause.' §8.4 then concludes 'THE CONSEQUENCE: this WEAKENS route 1 … One word, and it is the adverse one', on three independent grounds. Both can be true — 'the ask still stands' and 'the route is weaker' are different statements — but a reader who reads the headline learns only the first, and the section the paper itself calls 'the most consequential external finding in this document' is not represented there at all.
p1s.evidence: manuscript lines 47-83 (THE HEADLINE, two halves, no mention of §8) against §8 opening ('the most consequential external finding in this document') and §8.4 ('THE CONSEQUENCE: this WEAKENS route 1').
p1s.fix: Add a third half to the headline, three sentences: a 2026 peer-reviewed sarcoma ATR programme selects on HRD — the biomarker route 1's own source paper spends a figure refuting for the FET class — and it comes from the group ranked first for the wet-lab ask; the tier does not move and the rank is not re-set here, but the route is weaker and §8.4 says so.

p1s.summary: The title names one of the document's three deliverables and the paper twice tells the reader the other two matter more. The title is 'The in-silico ATR vulnerability assessment for EMC'; §2 opens 'This is the most consequential finding in the document AND IT IS NOT ABOUT ATR'; §8 opens 'the most consequential external finding in this document'. A referee asked to restate the central claim has to choose between an ATR-transfer assessment, a cell-line identity correction with repository-wide consequences, and a competing-biomarker landscape finding. Compounding this, roughly a third of the body (§2.3, §3.0, §3.0a, §3.2a, §3.3, §8.1's author-parsing bug, the Appendix) is a post-mortem of this project's own tooling defects — offered as evidence of rigour, and readable by an unsympathetic referee as evidence that the pipeline's outputs are not yet trustworthy, since two of those defects had already produced a published-then-retracted verdict and a sign error on the mechanism's load-bearing predictor.
p1s.evidence: manuscript title vs §2 first line and §8 first paragraph; Appendix rows for `NO_DDR_SIGNATURE_IN_EMC_TUMOURS`, for `ncbi_accessions_linked_to_a_gene: 0`, and for the GSE24369 contrast values whose ATM sign was wrong ('the sign was wrong on the mechanism's own load-bearing predictor').
p1s.fix: For an outward-facing version, split: the ATR transfer assessment is the paper; the H-EMC-SS identity finding is a short standalone note with its own title (it is independently useful and currently buried); the module post-mortems move to an SI or a methods appendix, one line each in the main text. If the document stays whole, the title must name all three.

p1s.summary: The document is written for a repository, not for an external reader, and most of its evidence pointers do not resolve outside it. It refers to 'this repository' and 'this repo', numbers its subject 'route 1' and '1b' by an internal ranking document, cites internal JSON and .py paths as relative links with no repository URL, and has no data-availability statement, no methods section separable from the narrative, and no reference list. A referee cannot check the central numbers without knowing where the artifact lives.
p1s.evidence: manuscript producer block (relative links to ../../modalities/*.json and *.py), §0, §2.3, §6.3 and §8.4 (route 1 / route 1b, 'this repository had already ranked'), absence of any http(s) link other than the two PubMed/doi links in §8.
p1s.fix: Add a data-and-code availability statement giving the public repository URL and the exact commit, so every relative path becomes resolvable; gloss 'route 1' once on first use as 'the ATR arm of this programme'; add the reference list called for above.

p2s.summary: The non-DDR control drugs are never named or counted in the manuscript. §5 says predictors had to clear 'specificity against non-DDR control drugs' and prints a mean; the set is paclitaxel and bortezomib — two drugs — plus doxorubicin, which has no data in this GDSC2 read and which would have been a poor 'non-DDR' control anyway, being a DNA-damaging topoisomerase II poison. A reader cannot judge a two-drug control they cannot see. Fix: name the drugs and the count in §5, and drop doxorubicin from the intended control set or justify it.
p2s.evidence: research/modalities/emc_atr_vulnerability.py line 2839 `non_ddr_controls = ("paclitaxel", "bortezomib", "doxorubicin")`; research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json#part_d_drug_response_correlation.gdsc_meta.drugs_with_data = [azd6738, bortezomib, mk-1775, olaparib, paclitaxel, talazoparib, ve-822] — no doxorubicin; manuscript grep for 'paclitaxel|bortezomib|doxorubicin' returns 0 hits.

p2s.summary: The FET-signature paragraph reports the association that fits the narrative and omits the larger one that does not. §5 says the held-out signature 'reproduces the PARP bound rather than escaping it … PARP-inhibitor sensitivity at −0.239' — the mean of olaparib −0.244 and talazoparib −0.235. The same signature's largest association in the panel is bortezomib at +0.265, a proteasome inhibitor with no DDR story, which suggests the signature is tracking something generic and drug-idiosyncratic rather than a DDR bound. Fix: report bortezomib in that paragraph, or state that the signature's largest association is to a non-DDR drug and that this limits what its PARP association can be read as.

§5's sample sizes drop without explanation. The header states '956 lines with ceralasertib/AZD6738 and 892 with berzosertib/VE-822'; the passing test then reports n 597 and n 565, and the expression predictors' n (704, 656) is never given at all. The drop is the intersection with the CRISPR and expression matrices, which is unobjectionable and unstated. Fix: one clause — 'n falls to 597/565 where CRISPR gene effects are also available, and to 704/656 for the expression predictors.'
p2s.evidence: manuscript §5 opening paragraph and the ✅ paragraph; research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json#part_d_drug_response_correlation.correlations['azd6738'].n_lines_with_residual = 956 vs .by_predictor[...].n = 597 (dependency) / 704 (expression).

p2s.summary: 'This is a reading of absence, not an absent reading' is claimed for DepMap's FILTERED fusion call set, and a filtered set is by construction a set with calls removed. §2.1's table argues that ACH-001519 being present in OmicsFusionFiltered.csv with two calls, neither naming a FET gene or NR4A3, is a positive reading of absence. It is strong evidence, but a filtered caller drops calls that fail its filters, so 'not in the filtered file' is weaker than 'not present in the sample'. The Cellosaurus caution, not the fusion caller, is what carries §2 — and §2.2's 'Established' statement is correctly bounded, so nothing downstream is wrong. Fix: qualify the ⭑ clause to 'a reading of absence in the FILTERED call set, which is not the same as absence from the unfiltered calls'.
p2s.evidence: manuscript §2.1 table, DepMap row; research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json#part_a_hemcss_identity.depmap_fusion_calls (_source 'DepMap OmicsFusionFiltered.csv', all_calls_verbatim ['AL158209.1--NEBL','VIM--RPS25']).

p2s.summary: The series-selection rule is honestly disclosed and then defended by an argument that makes it non-binding. §3.4 notes the fixed rule picked GSE4303 — 'That is NOT the better instrument' — and adds 'it does not matter here, because the two series agree'. They agree on the graded verdict but not on the raw contrast: GSE4303 puts three DDR concepts above the 0.2 threshold and GSE24369 puts nothing above 0.045. Also, only GSE4303's proliferation-adjusted column is printed; GSE24369's adjusted values are never shown. Fix: print GSE24369's adjusted column too, and say 'the two series agree on the verdict and differ substantially on the raw contrast' rather than 'agree'.
p2s.evidence: manuscript §3.4 tables; research/modalities/emc_atr_vulnerability.py lines 2140-2216 (`_rank_key` orders on readable platforms then n_EMC, and `readable` is set to the CHOSEN series' platforms only, so the verdict is computed from GSE4303 alone).

p2s.summary: Superlative inflation. Three different findings are each called the most important thing in the document: §2 'the most consequential finding in the document', §8 'the most consequential external finding in this document', §8.4 'the most informative single fact here'; §6.3 separately calls the ATM autophosphorylation experiment 'the most informative missing measurement'. Each is defensible in isolation; together they stop guiding the reader. Fix: keep one, demote the others to plain statements.
p2s.evidence: manuscript §2 opening, §8 opening, §8.4 point 3, §6.3 final rows.

p2s.summary: 'RGG dose-calibration prediction' in §0's 'what still stands' table is ambiguous in a direction the document forbids. The row never says what is being dosed; a reader can take 'dose-calibration' as a drug-dosing claim, which §6.2 item 2 explicitly disclaims. Fix: name the axes — 'the RG-dipeptide-content calibration curve published by the FET/ATR authors, on which EMC's fusions are placed' — so no dosing reading is available.
p2s.evidence: manuscript §0 headline table, row 3; §6.2 item 2 ('An effective concentration, dose, schedule or exposure. Nothing here is a potency measurement').

p2s.summary: 'the single best-fit collaborator in the world' (§8, opening) is a global superlative resting on an internal ranking document. Fix: 'the group this programme's own outreach ranking placed first' — same information, no unsupported universal.
p2s.evidence: manuscript §8 first paragraph and §8.4 point 3 ('ranked the USZ/Zurich group #1'), citing research/modalities/emc-atri-outreach-DRAFT.md.

p2s.summary: Frontmatter is stale and self-describing as unverified. `date: 2026-08-05` predates content the body dates to 2026-08-07 and later (the PMID 37205599 supersession, the hardening-round corrections in the Appendix); `last_verified: unverified`; `purpose: 'purpose was not stated separately when frontmatter was backfilled'`; `_backfilled: true`. MK-1775 aside (see the blocker), the WEE1-inhibitor response data is a free, unreported instrument. WEE1 appears in Part C's dependency table at gene effect −2.600 and is discussed in §8, and GDSC2 8.5 supplies MK-1775 response for 965 lines in the same read — so a WEE1 arm of Part D exists at $0 and is neither run nor declined. p2s.summary: GDSC LN_IC50 is used without addressing censoring, and AUC is not mentioned. GDSC fits IC50 values that frequently lie above the maximum screened concentration for insensitive lines, so LN_IC50 is extrapolated at the insensitive tail — the tail that matters most for a sensitivity correlation. The line-median residual correction mitigates general potency offsets but not extrapolation. Fix: state the choice and its limitation in §5, and if AUC is available in the same file, report the passing correlation against AUC as a robustness check.

A line-median correction removes each line's general drug sensitivity'); manuscript §5 opening paragraph; no occurrence of 'AUC', 'censor' or 'maximum concentration' in the document.

p2s.summary: No multiplicity statement in Part D. Four predictors x seven drugs x two specificity axes are computed and the ones reported are chosen after the fact; the four bars were pre-registered, which mitigates the predictor axis but not the drug axis. Fix: one sentence stating that the four predictors and their directions were fixed in advance and that no correction was applied across drugs, so nominal t-values are descriptive.

p2s.summary: 'Fixed before the numbers' is asserted three times and evidenced nowhere. §1 ('the grading, fixed before the numbers'), §3.4 ('The rule was not changed after the numbers landed') and §5 ('four bars fixed before the numbers'). The verbatim reproduction in the artifact shows the criteria match the code today, not that they preceded the results. The claim is cheap to evidence and expensive to assert. Fix: cite the commit sha and date at which GRADING_CRITERIA_VERBATIM, the 0.2 threshold, the four bars and `_rank_key` were committed, beside the first commit of the corresponding result.

objections_i_raised_and_the_paper_alread: PSEUDO-REPLICATION IN PART B — DROPPED. The t-values looked impossible for n=10 vs 6 (t 4.46 on Δ 0.311), which usually means genes are being treated as replicates. They are not: `_contrast` and `_adj_contrast` build one score per SAMPLE (the set's mean minus the sample's own background mean, over the sample's own SD) and run Welch over samples, refusing any group below n=3. The large t comes from genuinely small between-sample variance in a within-sample-standardised score. The method note in the artifact states this design explicitly. research/modalities/emc_atr_vulnerability.py lines 2022-2051 and derive_part_b's `_method` string.

CIRCULARITY OF THE HELD-OUT FET SIGNATURE — DROPPED. Derived only on the 962 lines with NO GDSC data (34 FET, 928 non-FET) and scored on the 965 that have it, with the design rationale written into the artifact and the caveat that it is a signature of the read subspace only. `_fet_signature_design` in research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json.

PART C'S COORDINATION NULL — DROPPED, and the paper made my objection before I could. I was going to say that 1/20 vs 3/71 bottom-quartile-on-all-three is being compared against a 0.25^3 independence expectation; §4 states 'The null there is the comparator's own fraction, NOT 0.25³ — ATR, ATRIP and CHEK1 are one signalling module and their gene effects are correlated by construction, so an independence-based expectation would err in the direction that flatters the hypothesis.' That is the correct analysis, stated against the paper's own interest.

'THE LINE-MEDIAN CORRECTION IS OVER SEVEN DRUGS, SO IT IS CIRCULAR' — REFUTED BY THE CODE. `line_median = df.groupby('_key')[ic_c].median()` is computed over the whole 242,036-row GDSC2 8.5 table BEFORE the frame is filtered to the seven drugs of interest, so the residual really is against each line's median over every GDSC drug, as §5 says. research/modalities/emc_atr_vulnerability.py lines 2637-2640.

'THE PAPER READS THE PART B NULL AS EVIDENCE AGAINST THE HYPOTHESIS' — IT DOES NOT, AND IT SAYS SO TWICE. §3.4's '⚠ What it is NOT' and §6.1's '⛔ WEAK is a statement about the TRANSCRIPTIONAL shadow of the hypothesis, not about the hypothesis' both state that no expression matrix can measure a recruitment-and-phosphorylation event at a double-strand break. That is the correct bound and it is not buried — it is a flagged paragraph in both places.

'THE ARGUMENT FROM SILENCE IN §8.4' — HALF ANSWERED. §8.4 point 3 makes 'the people holding the models and the assay did not reach for FET status' the most informative fact, and §8.5 item 5 then says 'That the authors rejected a FET framing. They did not address it. ⚠ Not addressing an idea and rejecting it are different, and only the first is observed.' The disclaimer is correct and prominent. It does not fully neutralise §8.4's rhetorical use, but the reader is given the tools to discount it, so this drops from an objection to a note.

'PART C IS BEING QUOTED AS EVIDENCE AGAINST THE HYPOTHESIS' — PRE-EMPTED. §4 closes '⛔ Reported as a failed instrument, and it must not be quoted as evidence against the hypothesis. A full knockout removes the protein everywhere; a sub-lethal inhibitor does not.' That is the right distinction and it is stated flatly rather than in a subordinate clause.
notes: One blocker, fifteen P1s, thirteen P2s. The blocker and the first two P1s are one family and share one fix: Part D reports drug-level means where the per-drug numbers disagree, and the per-drug numbers are all sitting in the committed artifact. Publishing §5's table with a per-drug rho column and a per-control-drug specificity column resolves the blocker, both averaging P1s and two P2s at once, and it changes no pre-registered verdict — the PASS stays a pass and the three failures stay failures. The central claim as stated in §6.1 ('the hypothesis is neither supported nor refuted here') is well supported and unusually carefully bounded; what is not supported is the interpretive sentence attached to the one passing test. The two structural P1s (the headline omitting §8.4, and a title naming one of three deliverables) are what a referee would raise first about the document as a whole, and neither is a science problem.
